newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium urges coherent world effort on Zaire. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Belgium urges coherent world effort on Zaire. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]

text.p: Belgium called for unity among those seeking a peaceful solution to the war in eastern Zaire and said international efforts to this end were making progress.
"It looks like there is progress and there will be an international effort. It is important the international community shows cohesion," Foreign Ministry spokesman Andre Querton said.

Talks began in Cape Town on Thursday to bring Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila and President Mobutu Sese Seko's chief security adviser, Ngbada Nzambo Ko Ayumba, together for a face-to-face meeting.
Querton condemned the government's bombing of rebel-held towns in eastern Zaire. "The solution to recovering territory which is yours is not bombing the civilian population."

On Monday the Zairean air force bombed towns in the east held by rebels who took up arms late last year after local authorities tried to expel them to their ancestral homeland Rwanda. About a dozen people were killed in the raids and thousands fled.

The war is intertwined with the conflict between Hutus and Tutsis in Rwanda. Hutu hardliners massacred up to 800,000 minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus in 1994 before fleeing en masse into Zaire as a Tutsi-led government seized power.

International efforts in December to help hundreds of thousands of refugees caught between government and rebel forces failed because of discord over how best to help, and were overtaken by events when many refugees decided to return to Rwanda.
But several hundred thousand uprooted Rwandans, as well as the local Zairean population, remain in the battle zone.
